thread:
incident-bot: [ALERT] Pager: inference-service 503-rate spike — paging @sre_sam @alex. Incident page: https://infra.redwood/incident/2367890123

sre_sam: ack, joining bridge now.

alex: on it, grabbing logs and checking model routing table.

maria: noticed dashboards show a sharp 5xx increase in eu-west about 11:42 UTC, courtesy metric spike on inference-proxy. I'm pulling customer-facing dashboards.

sre_sam: mitigation attempt 1: scaled inference pool to 8 replicas and enabled fallback routing to model-small. ran `kubectl scale deployment inference --replicas=8` and toggled routing policy to prefer variant B. monitoring...

deploy-bot: rolling restart of inference-proxy started @2367890200 and completed @2367890225. Logs: https://ci.redwood/job/infra/3162

kevin: quick question — was there a config merge earlier today? I see PR #4527 touched prefix cache TTL behavior for canary.

alex: yes that PR updated `cache.prefix_ttl` in the canary build. local canary had TTL=0 for a path, looking at the diff now:
```
- prefix_ttl: 300
+ prefix_ttl: 0  # accidental push from debug branch
```

maria: customer impact: three tenants reported degraded latency / 5xx (cust-orp1, portalx, govcorp). Support tickets #7892 and #7893 opened; both escalated to SEs. Approx degraded window ~11:42–11:54 UTC (~12m).

sre_sam: starting RCA doc skeleton. Proposed postmortem meeting: tomorrow 10:00 PT. Owners: timeline/alex, contributing-factors/kevin, impact/maria, mitigation/sre_sam, comms/jess_legal. I'll create calendar invite.

jess_legal: flagged govcorp SLA; I'll need early review of the external statement. Please include exact minutes of elevated errors and tenant IDs.

alex: drafting timeline now, uploading to doc. Preliminary timeline (UTC):
```
11:41:58 - canary merge deployed to proxy-canary
11:42:12 - dashboards show 5xx spike in eu-west
11:42:50 - incident-bot pages oncall
11:43:10 - oncall bridge created (sre_sam, alex)
11:44:00 - first mitigation: scale replicas + enable fallback routing
11:46:30 - 5xxs trending down, but intermittent failures continue
11:50:00 - rolling restart of inference-proxy initiated
11:54:20 - errors returned to baseline
```

maria: added ticket refs and customer notes to the doc (support links redacted). Also captured export of the error-rate graph.

kevin: root cause hypothesis: the canary change set inadvertently set a TTL to 0 which caused aggressive KV prefix eviction under load; combined with autoscaler lag (metric rolling window 60s) caused temporary capacity starvation. I'll add the canary diff and simulation logs to the contributing factors section.

alex: @deploy-bot can you attach the exact deploy diff and build tag used? need the SHA for the doc.

deploy-bot: Attachments uploaded: diff @sha:abc1234, build: inference-proxy:2026.03.15-rc1 (link: https://ci.redwood/artifacts/abc1234).

sre_sam: creating action items in JIRA INC-4532 to track follow-ups: 1) revert canary TTL change in config, 2) add unit/regression test for prefix ttl, 3) tighten canary merge checklist, 4) reduce autoscaler metric window from 60s->30s for this path. I'll add owners.

maria: also add customer comms draft to action items: short external blurb + targeted outreach to govcorp point-of-contact. @jess_legal hop on for review pls.

kevin: requesting peer review for my contributing-factors writeup. Please review before 16:00 PT so I can fold comments into final draft.

pm_ryan: product request: include a short blurb for the status page and a summary of what we changed to prevent recurrence. Keep it simple: cause, impact, mitigation, follow-ups.

alex: uploaded RCA draft (link: https://docs.redwood/rca/2367890123-draft). TAGGING: @kevin @maria @jess_legal @sre_sam — please comment inline.

jess_legal: quick review done — two copy edits on the public blurb and one suggestion to redact internal timings in public statement. Looks fine to sign off once we confirm exact customer minutes and JIRA tracking numbers.

sre_sam: sign-off checklist (internal): 1) timeline verified with logs (alex), 2) impact numbers confirmed (maria), 3) mitigation steps & evidence attached (sre_sam), 4) actions filed in JIRA (INC-4532), 5) legal review complete (jess_legal). I'll mark ready once #1-#5 are green.

alex: updated timeline with final log corroboration and added console screenshots. Marking #1 done.

maria: confirmed impact minutes against support tickets; added tenant-safe summary for public post. Marking #2 done.

kevin: added regression test PR and canary checklist items to the action list. PR link: https://git.redwood/pr/4589.

jess_legal: legal sign-off complete for external blurb with the suggested redactions.

sre_sam: all items green, I'm signing off on the internal RCA draft. Will schedule the postmortem review meeting and invite eng, sres, product, and legal.

alex: thx team. final note for writeup: keep causal chain tight (config -> eviction -> autoscaler lag -> transient capacity shortage) and be explicit about mitigation steps taken and timeline.

maria: short customer-facing summary draft (for support/SEs): "We experienced elevated 5xx errors for a subset of customers due to a configuration regression in a canary deploy. We rolled back the canary, scaled capacity, and applied a rolling restart. Three customers experienced degraded requests for ~12 minutes; all services restored. We're adding tests and changing autoscaler window to reduce recurrence risk."

kevin: i'll attach the simulation run that reproduces the TTL eviction at scale to the RCA.

sre_sam: closing notes: created JIRA INC-4532 with sub-tasks assigned, calendar invite for postmortem set for tomorrow 10:00 PT, doc link shared, legal + product looped. Great triage by oncall. :thumbsup:

maria: thanks all. We'll track action items in the JIRA and reopen if anything new shows up. :party_parrot:

alex: leaving final marker — please do the peer review and add thumbs up on the doc if you agree so we can mark the RCA final.

(react: alex +1, kevin :thumbsup:, jess_legal :white_check_mark:)
